title: --overwrite replaces a device node or FIFO given as --out (regression introduced by the RC-02 fix)
evidence: Sandbox run as root: '--out /dev/null --overwrite' exited 0 and left /dev/null as a regular 0600 file (stat: 'regular empty file'); every later '>/dev/null' wrote to that file. A FIFO given as --out was likewise replaced by a regular file. The guard tests isdir and lexists only; it never checks that an existing target is a regular file. Before the fix the tool opened --out for writing, which is harmless on /dev/null. I restored the node in the review container with mknod (c 1 3, mode 666). No test covers special files.
consequence: Discarding the report with the common '/dev/null' idiom breaks the host or CI container for every other process when run with privileges (agents and CI commonly run as root). Not a corpus-integrity defect: no input or original is touched.
reproduction: In a throwaway container only: python reconcile_judgments.py --incoming b.jsonl --repo <copy> --out /dev/null --overwrite; stat -c %F /dev/null. Safe variant: mkfifo f; same command with --out f; stat -c %F f
required_correction: Refuse an existing --out that is not a regular file (os.lstat + stat.S_ISREG) in check_out_path, also on the re-check; add tests for a FIFO and (skipped unless safe) a device path; state it in the README guard list.

title: With --overwrite the tool still replaces any non-input file under the repository, including frozen registers and other protected paths
evidence: Sandbox: '--out repo/legal_knowledge/audit_work/WS-B-JUDGMENTS/subsequent_treatment.csv --overwrite' exit 0, register replaced by the report. Only the five input kinds and any 'curated_originals' path component are refused. Crawler data/raw, data/meta, data/sections, data/text and registers that are not inputs are not refused. The README states this limit. Without --overwrite no existing file can be replaced (hard-link no-clobber confirmed).
consequence: A mistyped --out with --overwrite can destroy a frozen register or an immutable crawler file. The earlier required correction (refuse --out under the --repo root) was not adopted; it is disclosed rather than fixed.
reproduction: cp identity_resolution.csv <copy>/.../subsequent_treatment.csv; run with that --out and --overwrite; sha256sum before and after
required_correction: When --repo is given, refuse an existing --out under the repo root (or at least under data/ and legal_knowledge/ outside a named audit_work output folder), or require --overwrite targets to carry the tool's own report header.

title: Residual fail-open and exit-code cases on malformed input
evidence: (a) 100,000-deep nested JSON array raises an uncaught RecursionError: traceback, exit 1 (README says 2); no report written. (b) Non-string scalars are stringified and accepted: court=5, court=['Supreme Court'], parties=7, item_id=['a'] (written as "['a']"), case_numbers as a dict. (c) A UTF-8 BOM on a CSV batch turns the header into '\ufeffitem_id'; the item_id is silently dropped and replaced by 'line2' (exit 0). (d) Bidi override U+202E, zero-width and C1 controls (U+0085, U+009B) are accepted; a full-width '=' lead is not neutralised. (e) A 5 MB field is written to a report cell larger than the csv module's default field limit.
consequence: (a) not exit 2 as documented, though still fail closed. (b)(c) silently altered identifiers or metadata in a review artefact. (d)(e) reviewer-side display and tooling risk only.
reproduction: Batches built in the reviewer temp directory c8revC2_tmp/m (deep.jsonl, court_int.jsonl, itemid_list.jsonl, csv_bom.csv, bidi.jsonl, huge.jsonl); run with --repo <copy> --out <new file>
required_correction: Catch RecursionError (exit 2); require str for item_id, court, judgment_date, sha256, source_url and str or the documented object form for parties; open CSV with utf-8-sig or reject a BOM; extend CONTROL_RE to C1 and bidi controls; cap field length.
